name: mewing
blurb: Pressing your tongue to the roof of your mouth for a sharper jaw; also a "shh" gesture
title: Mewing Meaning: What Does Mewing Mean in Slang?
description: Mewing means holding your tongue against the roof of your mouth to sharpen the jaw. Named after orthodontists John and Mike Mew, it went viral in 2019.
answer: Mewing is the practice of pressing your whole tongue flat against the roof of your mouth, lips closed, in the belief that it will give you a sharper jawline over time. It is named after the British orthodontists John Mew and his son Mike Mew, whose "orthotropics" ideas spread on YouTube and went viral in 2019. In 2024 it turned into a classroom joke: kids put a finger to their lips, then trace their jaw, meaning "can't talk, I'm mewing". There is no good scientific evidence that it reshapes the face.

body: Literally, mewing is a tongue posture exercise. Supporters claim that keeping the tongue up and the mouth closed changes the face, making the jaw and cheekbones more defined. It is part of "looksmaxxing", online culture about maximising your looks.

In Gen Alpha slang, "mewing" is also a gesture and an excuse. A student who does not want to answer a question puts a finger to their lips in a "shh", then runs it along their jawline: "I can't talk, I'm mewing." It is a joke, often a cheeky way to ignore someone.

head: Date
Event
rows: Mike Mew starts the Orthotropics YouTube channel, explaining his and his father's tongue-posture ideas.
A forum post asks about results from "Mike Mewing", an early recorded use of the name.
Google searches for mewing rise from January; in March The Guardian calls it a YouTube craze.
UK and US media report teachers pushing back against students "mewing" in class.
Mike Mew is struck off the UK dental register.

body: John Mew, who developed orthotropics, had already lost his licence in 2017; he died in June 2025 at 96.

ul: "Why aren't you answering?" (finger to lips, trace jaw) "Mewing."
"I'm on a 30-day mewing streak." (joking about being serious about it)
"Bro is mewing in every photo." (someone always clenching their jaw for pictures)
Used next to other looksmaxxing slang such as mogging, and the Gigachad jaw as the "goal".

body: Orthodontists say there is no credible evidence that mewing changes the bone structure of the face, especially in adults whose bones have stopped growing; the American Association of Orthodontists has said it found no evidence it improves the jaw. Some people may look sharper simply because of posture in a photo.

body.note: Most kids who say "I'm mewing" are joking, not doing the exercise. Teachers have found the gesture rude when used to ignore them, and some have pushed back against it in class.

faq.a: After John Mew and Mike Mew, the British orthodontists behind "orthotropics", the theory the technique comes from.

faq.q: What does the mewing hand gesture mean?
faq.a: A finger to the lips ("shh") and then along the jawline means "I can't talk, I'm mewing". Kids use it as a joke or to dodge talking.

faq.q: Does mewing actually change your jawline?
faq.a: There is no reliable scientific evidence that it does. Orthodontists do not consider it a substitute for real treatment.
